matches.preview: The model gives Newcastle United a narrow advantage, with a home win at 44%, compared with 30% for Bournemouth and 26% for the draw. Looking back to last season, Newcastle won two of their final six league matches, while Bournemouth went unbeaten across their final six, with three wins and three draws. The recent head-to-head history also favours the visitors: Bournemouth won 2-1 at Newcastle in April and avoided defeat in all five listed meetings. On total goals, the model leans towards over 2.5 at 59%, against 41% for under 2.5.

The total-goals forecast is almost even, with a narrow lean towards over 2.5 goals at 51%, against 49% for under 2.5.
